name: Fireweave
description: Fireweave is an AI release engineer. Developer docs: SDKs for Node, Python, Go, Java, Rust, and the browser, plus onboarding for the CLI, Terraform, and coding-agent plugins.

instructions: Official Fireweave documentation. Brand casing in prose is 'Fireweave'. 'FireWeave-HQ' appears only inside GitHub URLs and the Terraform registry address, which are identifiers — never change those.
Product noun is control point. The wire protocol, Decision envelopes, conformance fixtures, and capabilities.features.flags still use flagKey — do not invent controlPointKey.

SDK v1 (ADR-0010) exposes exactly two capabilities: control-point reads and target registration. The OpenFeature providers (FireweaveProvider, FireweaveWebProvider), makeFireweaveLocalProvider, and the releases, exposures, signals, capabilities, and guardrails namespaces were all removed. Do not document them as available APIs.
The Node package is @fireweaveai/server-sdk. The old @fireweaveai/sdk is frozen at 2.1.0 and must never be presented as the install target.
mode is a required init option and is never inferred — 'remote' or 'local'. Remote without credentials is a boot error.
No SDK reads environment variables. Credentials are explicit init options in every language. FW_DEPRECATION_WARNINGS no longer exists.
registerTarget exists on all seven SDKs, including Go and Java. Go exposes ControlPoints(); Java exposes controlPoints(), getNumberValue, and getObjectValue.
The flags alias shares identity with controlPoints. It is silent at runtime in every language except Python, which logs one deprecation notice per process.
Wire paths: all seven remote adapters implement /v1/flags/evaluate and /v1/targets/register. Only the Node and Web adapters implement /v1/capture.
Terraform uses FIREWEAVE_API_KEY and FIREWEAVE_ENDPOINT — not the SDK's FW_ variables. There are no reusable Fireweave Terraform modules.

Do not invent APIs, packages, env vars, endpoints, or CLI commands. Never present an unpublished artifact as installable — the Swift SDK exists in-tree but is not distributable. Do not document rollout-ci as generally available, or console-only features such as guardrails and ramp controls.
